failures.title: BMW N54B30 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: High-Pressure Fuel Pump (HPFP) & Piezo Injector Failure - 2006-2010 models
items.whatHappens: The N54B30 uses a high-pressure direct injection system with piezoelectric injectors and a mechanical HPFP. The HPFP is prone to internal cam wear, causing extended cranking, misfires, and limp mode. Worse, failing piezo injectors can leak diesel directly into the cylinders, washing the cylinder walls, diluting the engine oil, and ultimately leading to catastrophic bearing failure or hydrolock.
items.repairVsReplace: Standalone HPFP and injector replacement can cost £1,500-£3,000. However, if injector leakage has already caused severe cylinder scoring or bearing damage, a full BMW N54B30 engine replacement is the only viable route.

items.title: Turbocharger Wastegate Rattle & Boost Leaks - 80,000+ miles
items.whatHappens: The twin turbochargers suffer from wastegate pivot wear, creating a distinct metallic rattling noise on cold starts and under light throttle. Additionally, the plastic charge pipe and vacuum lines become brittle and crack, leading to boost leaks, lean running conditions, and turbo over-speeding.
items.repairVsReplace: Upgraded aluminium charge pipes and wastegate repair kits are common fixes (£400-£900). If the turbo cores have suffered shaft play or oil seal failure from over-speeding, the turbos must be rebuilt or replaced, which is standard practice on a fully reconditioned N54B30.

items.title: Timing Chain & Guide Wear - Higher mileage examples
items.whatHappens: While not as universally fatal as the N47/N57 rear-chain designs, the N54's front-mounted timing chain and plastic guides can stretch and wear at higher mileages, presenting as a cold-start rattle.
items.repairVsReplace: A chain kit replacement is a standard maintenance item. Read our full timing chain failure guide.

failures.goodYearsLine: The N54B30 was only produced until 2010 before being replaced by the single-turbo N55. Early 2007-2008 models carry the highest risk of original-spec HPFP and injector failures, whereas late 2009-2010 units often benefited from mid-cycle technical updates to the fuel system and engine loom .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the N54B30
variants.intro: The N54B30 can be identified by the engine code stamped on the engine block (typically near the bell housing or on the front face), listed on your V5C registration document (Section D.2), or via a VIN decoder. It is most commonly confused with the single-turbo N55B30A that replaced it, and the newer modular B58B30M0. Fitting the wrong revision will result in severe ECU mapping mismatches, incorrect twin-turbo plumbing, and mounting point discrepancies, as the N54 requires specific DME software and parallel turbo exhaust manifolds.

relatives.description: - the single-turbo successor that resolved many of the N54's fuel system vulnerabilities, simplified the turbo plumbing, and moved the timing chain to the front of the engine for easier access.
- the modern modular 3.0-litre turbo that eventually replaced the N55; it uses a completely different architecture and is not a direct swap for the N54.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement BMW N54B30 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used BMW N54B30 is an extreme gamble unless it comes with comprehensive, documented proof that the HPFP, all six piezo injectors, and the turbo wastegates have been replaced or upgraded within the last 20,000 miles. Without this history, the risk of inheriting a fuel-system failure that destroys the bottom end is exceptionally high. Explore our vetted used engine network.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the baseline recommendation for the N54B30. A proper reconditioning process must systematically test and replace the piezo injectors, upgrade the HPFP to the latest revision, address the turbo wastegate rattle, and replace the timing chain and guides. This directly addresses the engine's most common failure points while restoring factory compression. View reconditioned BMW N54B30 options.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is highly justified if the host vehicle is a desirable E92 335is, E60 535i, or E71 X6 where long-term ownership or high-performance tuning is planned. An upgraded rebuild should include forged internals, upgraded rod bearings (a known weak point under boost), and a modernised fuel system to ensure longevity. Compare rebuilt BMW N54B30 specialists.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Choosing a supply-and-fit service through our network ensures the engine is installed by a specialist familiar with the N54's complex twin-turbo plumbing, charge pipe upgrades, and DME coding requirements, backed by a nationwide warranty. Learn more about supply and fit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The N54B30 is typically found in vehicles valued between £5,000 and £18,000, with early E90 335i and E60 535i examples often sitting at the lower end of this band. Because a fully reconditioned replacement can cost upwards of £4,780 fitted, the replacement cost can approach or exceed 60% of the vehicle's value on older, higher-mileage examples. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing .

items.question: What is the most common failure with the BMW N54B30 engine?
items.answer: The dominant failure is high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) and piezo injector failure, typically occurring between 60,000 and 100,000 miles. Failing piezo injectors can leak fuel into the cylinders, washing the cylinder walls and diluting the engine oil, which can lead to catastrophic bearing failure. A proper reconditioned unit will systematically test and replace the piezo injectors and upgrade the HPFP. Turbo wastegate rattle is also common but rarely writes off the engine block itself.

items.question: Which BMW models use the N54B30 engine?
items.answer: The BMW N54B30 was widely fitted to performance 35i and 40i models including the 1 Series (E82/E88), 3 Series (E90/E92/E93), 5 Series (E60/E61 and early F10), 6 Series (E63/E64), 7 Series (F01/F02), X6 (E71), and Z4 (E89) between 2006 and 2010. It powers various 135i, 335i, 535i, and xDrive35i badges, producing between 302 hp and 322 hp. Always verify your exact fitment using your registration number.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned BMW N54B30 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned BMW N54B30 is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the extreme risk of inherited HPFP and piezo injector wear. Used engines (£2,000-£3,500) are only viable if they come with comprehensive, documented proof that the injectors and fuel pump were recently replaced. Reconditioned units (£4,000-£7,000) systematically address the fuel system and turbo wastegates, offering a 12- to 24-month warranty. Rebuilt units provide forged internals for those planning high-performance tuning.
